Bloomberg reports that Apple plans to launch an OLED-equipped iPad mini before October, and has shared the company's expected timeline for updates to the entry-level iPad, iPad Air, and iPad Pro. Details below.

"The biggest iPad mini redesign in half a century"

Although rumours of the next-generation iPad mini featuring an OLED display have been circulating for some time, with an expected launch later this year, Bloomberg has now provided a more precise release timeframe.

According to the latest report, "Apple is preparing to unveil a new OLED version of the iPad mini (internal code name J510) as early as this autumn, with sales planned to begin in October." The report also notes that Apple will "eventually upgrade the iPad Air to an OLED display," but has "no plans to bring OLED to the entry-level iPad in the near term, which will continue to use the more affordable LCD technology."

Earlier this week, Weibo leaker yeux1122 also stated that the iPad mini will adopt an OLED display, but claimed there will be no ProMotion support, with the refresh rate remaining fixed at 60Hz.

Returning to the Bloomberg report, it points out that adding OLED may further push up the price of the iPad mini. The device currently starts at US$599, higher than the US$499 it was priced at before Apple made sweeping adjustments across its product line pricing a few weeks ago.

The report also shared Apple's expected timeline for its remaining iPad product lines:

According to people familiar with the matter, a new entry-level iPad (internal code name J581) is expected to launch as early as the first quarter of next year. The main change will be a faster processor rather than a major design overhaul. The new iPad Air will continue to be available in 11-inch and 13-inch versions, with internal code names J807 and J837, expected to debut in spring. Apple is also planning to launch new iPad Pro models around the same time, as Bloomberg News reported last month.

Finally, Bloomberg reiterated its report from a few days ago, stating that Apple is expected to update the Apple Pencil next year, with the new model potentially featuring a replaceable battery design.
